author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Russell Crowe premiered a documentary about his lifelong involvement in music at the Venice Film Festival on Friday. “What Love Builds” uses performance footage, archival material and Crowe's reflections to show how music has developed alongside an acting career best known for films including “Gladiator” and “A Beautiful Mind.”

Crowe performs with Indoor Garden Party, a group whose sound draws from rock, blues, country and gospel. The documentary grew from an idea first considered about 15 years ago and from an unusually large personal archive. Reuters reported that the production had accumulated roughly 18 million feet of footage documenting rehearsals, concerts and the relationships around Crowe's musical work.

The film screened out of competition in Venice, positioning it as a personal career portrait rather than an awards entry in the festival's main contest. Crowe, now 62, remains active on screen while preparing a 2027 European tour with the band. The documentary's central argument is that his music is not a side project attached to celebrity, but a continuous creative pursuit that predates and accompanies his film career.
dek: “What Love Builds” combines performances, archives and personal reflections to trace the actor's decades-long parallel career in music.
headline: Russell Crowe music documentary premieres in Venice
